thread.title: Extends Declines, Pulling Chip Stocks Lower, as Tech Sags on China Concern

author: Martin Baccardax
title: Extends Declines, Pulling Chip Stocks Lower, as Tech Sags on China Concern

organizations.name: tech sags on china concern apple inc.

text:
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) shares to a fresh 20-month low Thursday, pulling chip stocks lower and dragging the Nasdaq Composite into to bear market territory, after a shock the world's biggest tech company.

Cook pinned the weaker iPhone demand in China on several factors, including a slowing economy worsened by "rising trade tensions with the United States" and cited dollar, fewer carrier subsidies and customers taking advantage of reduced battery replacements in the softened demand for new iPhones.
"We have been cautious surrounding the newly launched iPhone's ability to drive an upgrade cycle, particularly in China, and December quarter results are worse than we would have expected," wrote BMO Capital Markets analyst Tim Long. "A less compelling new lineup that is priced well above competitive products, coupled with trade tensions, will probably mean more tough quarters ahead for the China business."
Apple shares were marked 8.2% lower at $144.90 Thursday, the lowest since April 2017 and a move that extends the stock's three-month loss to around 38.6% and values the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech giant at just over $690 billion- down from $1.1 trillion on October 3.

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaOne) January 3, 2019 Apple alone clipped around 106 points from the at the opening bell, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 180 points to take the tech-focused benchmark's slide from its August 29 peak to just over 20%.
Chipmakers wer also under pressure, with AMD ( AMD ) down 7.3%, Micron ( MU ) falling 4.2% and Nvidia ( NVDA ) sliding 4.2% from their prior close as investors clipped sales and earnings estimates based on a weaker holiday quarter for the world's third biggest smartphone maker.
Apple's German-listed units were marked 8.3% lower at €127.40, while Apple's European supply chain led the tech stock slump, with ASML NV ( ASML ) falling 3.4% in Amsterdam and Austrian chipmaker AMS AG ( AMSSY ) plunging 20%. STMicroelectronics ( STM ) was marked 8.65% lower while Anglo-German Dialog Semiconductor ( DLGNF ) fell 8.4% by mid-afternoon trading.
Stocks in Apple's global supply chain were also notably weaker in early trading, with Taiwan Semiconductor Holdings ( TSM ) falling 4.8%, Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ) down 8.5% and Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) down 6.8%.
Apple chipmaker Qorvoa ( QRVO ) slumped 8.4% to $58 per share while Universal Display ( OLED ) was seen 8.9% lower at $83.06 each
Apple CEO Tim Cook said late Wednesday that revenue for the three months ending in December would come in around $84 billion, notably shy of the Street consensus of around $91.5 cited dollar, fewer carrier subsidies and customers taking advantage of reduced battery replacements in the softened demand for new iPhones.
